title: Fire & Smoke Mitigation Final Invoice, Due Date and Job Closing
content:
Billing office clause for the Fire & Smoke Mitigation final invoice: when it is issued, what it totals, how its due date is set, and when the job closes.

## Clause

> The job must be in cleaning complete status when the final invoice is issued. The final invoice amount is the total of every charge line, and the payment due date is the invoice date plus the self-pay or insurance payment terms by funding source, in calendar days. The job closes when its balance due is exactly zero after invoicing.

## 1. Issuing the final invoice

1.1 The final invoice is issued only while the job is in cleaning complete status. Issuing it moves the job from cleaning complete to invoiced and records the invoice date, the total charges and the payment due date on the job.

1.2 The final invoice amount is the total of every charge line on the job: service call, securing, equipment day, cleaning and labor lines, and any other charge line booked to the job.

## 2. The payment due date

2.1 The due date is the invoice date plus the job's payment terms in calendar days, the terms being chosen by the job's funding source:

| Funding source on the job | Terms read from the job's tier |
|---|---|
| self-pay | the self-pay payment terms |
| insurance claim | the insurance payment terms |

2.2 Calendar days count every day, weekends and holidays included.

Hypothetical due date: an invoice dated 20 January under a hypothetical term of 20 calendar days falls due on 9 February (11 days to the end of January, then 9 days into February).

## 3. The balance due

The balance due is the amount the customer owes on one Fire & Smoke Mitigation job: charges and refunds raise it; customer payments, insurance postings and credits lower it.

## 4. Closing

4.1 The job closes when its balance due is exactly zero after invoicing. Closing moves the job from invoiced to closed and records the closing date.

| Job status | Balance due | Closing condition met? |
|---|---|---|
| invoiced | exactly 0.00 | yes, the job closes |
| invoiced | above 0.00 | no |
| invoiced | below 0.00 (a credit balance) | no |
| cleaning complete, not yet invoiced | 0.00 | no, the invoice has not been issued |

## Hypothetical illustration

A hypothetical job carries a service call line of 250.00, equipment day lines totalling 600.00 and cleaning lines totalling 990.00. Its final invoice amount is the total of those lines, 1840.00. If customer payments of 1840.00 are later posted after invoicing and nothing else is booked, the balance due reaches exactly zero and the job closes.
